historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 4.4 V8 launched in the Discovery lineup, it provided a powerful, torque-rich alternative to the inline-six diesels, becoming highly sought after for heavy towing and serious off-road capability.

milestones.description: 368DT (4.4L TDV8, 306hp) introduced in the Discovery 3 (L319), offering robust low-end torque and a twin-turbo setup.
368DT carried over to the Discovery 4 (L319) with minor emissions and ECU refinements to meet Euro 4/5 standards.
448DT (4.4L SDV8, 339hp) introduced as a premium upgrade, featuring improved oil cooling and a more robust bottom end to resolve early 368DT crankshaft concerns.
4.4 V8 phased out in the UK Discovery lineup, replaced by the 3.0L TDV6/SDV6 (306DT) for improved fuel economy and emissions compliance.

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The 4.4 V8 engines dominating the Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 are legendary for their towing capability, but early iterations are susceptible to specific mechanical stresses. Rebuilt 368DT and 448DT engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Crankshaft Stress - Why the Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 368DT Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Early timing chain tensioner design flaws combined with high towing loads can lead to chain stretch and, in severe cases, crankshaft fracture.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the timing chains, guides, and upgraded tensioners.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable only if the crankshaft and bearings show zero signs of wear or scoring.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt 368DT/448DT with upgraded bottom-end components and a 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if crankshaft scoring is present or the engine has suffered catastrophic failure.

problems.recommendation: If your Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 is an early 368DT model showing timing chain rattle, a full rebuilt unit with upgraded components is often the safest long-term investment. For later 448DT models with minor oil cooler leaks, a specialist seal replacement is highly cost-effective, provided the bottom end remains healthy.

problems.h4: Oil Cooler & Cooling System Leaks - Why the Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 448DT Loses Pressure
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler seals located in the valley of the V8 degrade over time, leading to oil leaks that can contaminate the turbocharger or cause low oil pressure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removing the inlet manifold to replace oil cooler O-rings and coolant crossover pipes.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly cost-effective if caught early and the bottom end remains healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt 448DT with revised cooling components and a 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if oil starvation has caused bearing spin or turbo destruction.

items.question: How much does a Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned or rebuilt 4.4 V8 engine for the Discovery typically costs between £5,500 and £12,000 for the supply-only unit in the UK.
keyPoints: Used 4.4 V8 engines start around £3,000 but carry higher risk due to age.
Rebuilt units with upgraded timing components sit at the £7,000-£12,000 mark.
Supply and fit labour will add £910-£1,560 depending on the specialist.
items.cta: -> Get free quotes for your Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 engine replacement.

items.question: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8?
items.answer: The 368DT engine is prone to timing chain tensioner wear, which can escalate to catastrophic failure if ignored. Watch for early warning signs.
keyPoints: A distinct metallic rattling or slapping noise from the engine bay on cold starts.
Engine management lights indicating cam/crank correlation faults.
Sudden loss of power or metallic knocking from the lower engine block.
items.cta: -> Compare specialist quotes to fix your Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 timing chain.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8?
items.answer: Yes, particularly for later Discovery 4 SDV8 models, which hold their classic status and market value exceptionally well.
keyPoints: Discovery 4 SDV8 models regularly sell for £8,000 to £18,000+.
An £8,000-£12,000 rebuilt engine preserves the vehicle's towing capability and long-term usability.
Early Discovery 3 models under £5,000 should be evaluated carefully against scrap value.
items.cta: -> Check current Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 replacement costs.

items.question: What is the difference between the 368DT TDV8 and 448DT SDV8 engines?
items.answer: Both are 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 diesels, but the 448DT was introduced as a refined, more robust evolution of the 368DT.
keyPoints: The 448DT features an upgraded oil cooling system and revised bottom-end components to prevent the crankshaft issues seen in early 368DT units.
items.cta: -> Get quotes for the correct engine for your Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8.

items.question: How long does a Land Rover Discovery 4.4 V8 engine replacement take?
items.answer: Because the 4.4 V8 is a densely packed twin-turbo engine, a specialist workshop requires careful extraction and specific Land Rover diagnostic tools.
keyPoints: Engine removal and refitting usually takes 14 to 18 hours of labour.
Total workshop turnaround is typically 4 to 6 working days, including ECU coding and adaptation.
